verdict.rationale: Gmail filters let users define rules that check incoming messages against criteria such as sender, subject, or size, and then automatically add or remove labels or forward the message. The only documented trigger is an incoming message matching the rule, and the documented actions are limited to labeling and forwarding. Push notifications are just a developer building block and earn no credit. Missing for 10: triggers beyond incoming-message matching, a broader set of automatic actions, and independent or hands-on corroboration of filter automation depth.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: When a message matches, filters automatically trigger actions such as adding or removing labels, or forwarding the email to a specified address.
Advanced rules configured for an account that evaluate incoming messages against specific matching criteria (like sender, subject, or size).
After you search, you can use the results to set up a filter for these messages.
